rows.title: Why some see the dollar's drop as a sign America is losing its financial might
rows.standfirst: The dollar has just posted its worst first-half of a year since 1973. And now investors wonder — is it a sign that America is losing its financial standing?

rows.title: Everything to know about Trump's tariff letters — and why it's a radical approach
rows.standfirst: President Trump this week has been firing off letters to global leaders that threaten new, high tariff rates and also announcing them via social media. Here's what has happened so far.

rows.title: Defunct oil wells are a national problem. Finding them is the first step
rows.standfirst: There could be about a million 'orphan' oil and gas wells across the U.S. As they age, they can leak greenhouse gases or unhealthy chemicals.

rows.title: Why can't we insure trees?
rows.standfirst: In the U.S., we insure most everything we sell. So why not trees? Today on the show why trees aren't insured like other crops, and what it would take to get that insurance with extreme weather events on the rise.

rows.title: 'Buy now, pay later' purchases can now affect your credit score. Here's what that means
rows.standfirst: Services that split up payments into installments are increasingly popular, especially among young and low-to-middle income shoppers. But now the FICO credit scoring company will be tracking that debt.

rows.title: Why is the dollar off to a weak start this year?
rows.standfirst: The U.S. dollar had its worst start this year in more than half a century. Harvard University economics professor Kenneth Rogoff says President Trump is accelerating the decline.

rows.title: One of the cheapest ways to save a life is going away (EXTENDED VERSION)
rows.standfirst: This episode was first published as a bonus episode for our Planet Money+ listeners. Today, we're making it available for everyone!

rows.title: Congress passed no tax on tips in Trump's 'big, beautiful bill.' Here's how it works
rows.standfirst: Congress passed the tax cut and spending megabill with President Trump's legislative priorities which includes new tax exemptions for tipped hourly workers. But how will it work?

rows.title: China Works to Dominate in AI and EV
rows.standfirst: The reality of China's efforts to lead in two important tech sectors. In artificial intelligence, control of the data needed to train new models could dictate where the industry is able to expand fastest. And a price war in China's electric vehicle industry.

rows.title: How ICE crackdowns are affecting the workforce
rows.standfirst: The Trump administration's crackdown on immigrants might be the most profound change in the American labor market right now. Industries that rely on immigrant labor are especially vulnerable, as ICE continues to raid businesses believed to have unauthorized workers.

rows.title: The U.S. labor market remains solid, with employers adding 147,000 jobs last month
rows.standfirst: U.S. employers added 147,000 jobs in June as the unemployment rate dipped to 4.1%. Job gains were concentrated in health care and state and local government.

rows.title: An Alabama food bank braces for big increase in demand if SNAP cuts take effect
rows.standfirst: The food assistance program known as SNAP could face significant reductions if President Trump's tax and spending bill passes the House.

rows.title: A thought experiment on how to fix the national debt problem
rows.standfirst: There's an economic fantasy you sometimes hear in D.C. It often gets trotted out when politicians are trying to add billions or trillions to the national debt. They claim that all the new spending will be worth it in the end because we will supercharge economic growth.

rows.title: CBS is the latest news giant to bend to Trump's power
rows.standfirst: With a $16 million payment to settle President Trump's lawsuit over 60 Minutes' interview with Kamala Harris, CBS becomes the latest media outlet to bow to his power.

rows.title: Why the Federal Reserve's building renovations are attracting the White House's ire
rows.standfirst: The Fed's $2.5 billion headquarters renovation is attracting mounting criticism from the Trump administration, which had been already attacking the central bank for not cutting interest rates.

rows.title: Trump's Brazil tariffs are 'grotesquely illegal,' says Nobel Prize-winning economist
rows.standfirst: Nobel Prize-winning economist Paul Krugman believes tariffs President Trump has threatened to impose on countries, including Mexico and Brazil, are here to stay and will cost U.S. consumers.

rows.title: Trump to meet with NATO over Russia-Ukraine war. And, a list of Trump's tariff letters
rows.standfirst: Trump will meet with NATO's secretary-general to discuss the Russia-Ukraine war as his frustrations grow over the conflict. And, the president says the European Union and Mexico will face 30% tariffs.

rows.title: A lawsuit against Tesla and its driver-assistance technology goes to trial in Florida
rows.standfirst: The case, which stems from a deadly crash in 2019, raises broader questions about the safety of Tesla's driver-assistance systems and whether the company has exaggerated their capabilities.

rows.title: Before La La Land, there was Fort Lee, New Jersey
rows.standfirst: Hollywood, baby! The glitz! The glamour! The ever-changing business models! This week, The Indicator is going to the movies. Starting today with the history of Hollywood and where it began ... New Jersey!

rows.title: 'Panicking': Why recent college grads are struggling to find jobs
rows.standfirst: Recent college graduates are facing one of the most challenging job markets in years — with the exception of the pandemic period — even as the overall unemployment rate remains low.

rows.title: Trump announces 30% tariffs against EU, Mexico to begin August 1
rows.standfirst: President Donald Trump on Saturday announced he's levying tariffs of 30% against the European Union and Mexico.

rows.title: Made in America
rows.standfirst: What people might picture when they think of "Made in America" ... might not look like the "Made in America" we have today.

rows.title: Preliminary report says fuel switches were cut off before Air India Boeing 787 crash
rows.standfirst: Indian investigators determined the Boeing 787 Dreamliner was properly configured and lifted off normally. But three seconds after takeoff, the engines' fuel switches were cut off.

rows.title: What Trump's One Big Beautiful Bill Act means for taxes on Social Security
rows.standfirst: Many Americans received an email from the Social Security Administration applauding the megabill's passage. Experts say it was misleading.

rows.title: Red tape indicators: sports betting, R&D and click-to-cancel
rows.standfirst: We are back with Indicators of the Week! Today, we'll be digging into why U.S. professional gamblers are worried about their future, why businesses might start investing more in research and development, and why cancelling your subscriptions is going to remain difficult.

rows.title: This TikTok video is fake, but every word was taken from a real creator
rows.standfirst: TikTok researchers and users say there is yet another type of deception to look out for on the hit video app: deepfake videos that copy the exact words of a real creator but in a different voice.

rows.title: Nutella-maker Ferrero to gobble up cereal giant Kellogg for $3.1 billion
rows.standfirst: Italian candy giant Ferrero offered the American breakfast company a $3.1 billion deal too sweet to pass up.

rows.title: Could Meta do more to protect us from cyber scams?
rows.standfirst: Many small businesses are online now, but so are cyber criminals trying to take advantage. On today's show, how one bar owner fell victim to a Facebook scam and if big tech could do more to protect small business owners from increasing cyber attacks. Read Stephan's original piece.

rows.title: Trump sets 50% tariff rate for Brazil, blasting treatment of former far-right president
rows.standfirst: President Trump defended former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro, who is accused of plotting an attempted coup following his loss in the 2022 election.

rows.title: U.S. coffee drinkers and businesses will pay the price for Trump's Brazil tariffs
rows.standfirst: President Trump plans to levy a 50% tariff on all goods from Brazil — the source of about 30% of U.S. coffee imports. This looming tariff threat has sent shock waves through the U.S. coffee industry.

rows.title: Your tinned fish obsession is helping resurrect a lost industry
rows.standfirst: Once upon a time, the states had a thriving tinned fish market. Like a lot of U.S. manufacturing though, that's been lost. But sardines are having a moment right now and that may help a growing effort to resurrect this lost industry.

rows.title: Bonus episode: The Indicator plays... movie business trivia!
rows.standfirst: To cap off our weeklong series on all things Hollywood, we're going to have a little fun! Tune in to hear Adrian, Darian and Wailin battle it out as they try to name movies based on cryptic descriptions of the businesses featured in them. You can play along!

rows.title: The week when crypto won big in America
rows.standfirst: Congress passed the first major crypto legislation in the U.S., marking a major milestone for the digital currency sector. And with President Trump's support, the industry plans to march on.

rows.title: Should you buy it? If you answer 'yes' to these questions, probably not
rows.standfirst: Sometimes we want to buy things we want, not what we need, and that's OK. When you're unsure whether to swipe that card or walk away, this guide can help you make a mindful decision you won't regret.

rows.title: Why are we so obsessed with manufacturing?
rows.standfirst: It seems like politicians cannot agree on a lot. But many seem to agree on... manufacturing. Leaders of both political parties have been working to try and make the U.S. a manufacturing powerhouse again.

rows.title: Besides bold letters to world leaders, Trump is working on a subtler tariff strategy
rows.standfirst: President Trump and his administration have been studying new sectoral tariffs that could cover a broad part of the American economy.

rows.title: How bipartisan support for public media unraveled in the Trump era
rows.standfirst: "It will test every single shred of creativity we have to continue to try to serve our mission," says one public media executive, as Congress ends federal funding for public broadcasting.

rows.title: Are you not entertained ... by our movie-related indicators?
rows.standfirst: The movies come to Indicators of the Week. We dig into why one film is letting you reserve tickets a whole year in advance, what ticket prices might tell us about tariffs and inflation, and how Los Angeles might be cutting back on the red tape when it comes to making movies there.

rows.title: CBS will end 'The Late Show with Stephen Colbert' next year
rows.standfirst: Colbert confirmed the cancellation during a show taping on Thursday. CBS said the move was "purely a financial decision against a challenging backdrop in late night."

rows.title: Settlement reached in investors' lawsuit against Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and other company leaders
rows.standfirst: A settlement has been reached in a class action investors' lawsuit against Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and company leaders over claims stemming from the privacy scandal involving Cambridge Analytica.

rows.title: A 'Crypto Week' win: Congress passes 1st major crypto legislation in the U.S.
rows.standfirst: It was a remarkable win for the crypto industry — and for President Trump, who campaigned on making the country "the crypto capital of the planet."

rows.title: How did Condé Nast go from dominance to decline? A new book explains
rows.standfirst: For decades, Condé Nast publications such as Vogue and Vanity Fair were consequential tastemakers. Writer Michael Grynbaum explores the heyday of these magazines and how they lost their footing.

rows.title: A well-run economy needs an independent Federal Reserve, says former reserve bank head
rows.standfirst: Former president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Loretta Mester says it's important that the Fed stays independent and that fiscal politics should not interfere with monetary policy makers and their decisions.

rows.title: Why more residents are saying 'No' to AI data centers in their backyard
rows.standfirst: The world's highest concentration of data centers is in Virginia. Many residents are not happy about that.

rows.title: The White House sets a swath of new tariff rates — and a new date — for dozens of countries
rows.standfirst: An executive order says most of the tariffs will not take effect for at least a week, despite an earlier assertion that new rates would take effect on Friday. Some goods from Canada would get a new 35% tariff rate beginning Friday, though.

rows.title: A fact checker hangs up his Pinocchios
rows.standfirst: "In an era where false claims are the norm, it's much easier to ignore the fact-checkers." Those are the final words of the final column of Glenn Kessler, who has been The Fact Checker at the Washington Post these last 14 years.

rows.title: Brazil Braces for Trump's Tariffs. Brits Say Goodbye to Ozzy
rows.standfirst: The threat of 50% US tariffs on some goods have Brazilian growers and producers are on edge. Heavy metal hero Ozzy Osbourne has a hometown farewell in Birmingham, England.

rows.title: High Noon is recalling some vodka seltzers mislabeled as Celsius energy drinks
rows.standfirst: Some beach variety packs of High Noon hard seltzers included canned cocktails mislabeled as blue raspberry Celsius energy drinks. The affected lots were sent to retailers in six states last week.

rows.title: What Trump's threat to tariff Russia's trade partners means for India
rows.standfirst: President Trump said India would pay the price for buying Russian oil and military equipment. Here is a look at how India, with one of Asia's largest economies, is responding.

rows.title: The Fed holds interest rates steady. And, Texas releases bid for new redistricting map
rows.standfirst: The Federal Reserve voted yesterday to keep interest rates steady, despite the president calling for lower rates. And, Texas Republicans proposed a new redistricting map.

rows.title: Not enough money for retirement? NPR wants to hear from you
rows.standfirst: Many adults over age 50 either have no retirement savings or worry they won't be able to support themselves during their post-working years. If that's you, NPR wants to hear your story.

rows.title: Online news publishers face 'extinction-level event' from Google's AI-powered search
rows.standfirst: While many factors often drive traffic fluctuations, publishers say the introduction of Google's AI Overviews has led to dramatic declines for news outlets and other online information sources.

rows.title: Why the Fed could lose $1.5 trillion
rows.standfirst: The Fed is on the hook for an estimated one-and-a-half trillion dollars. Despite the recent headlines, that's not because of building renovations. It's a much larger cost blowout caused by big actions taken during the pandemic to help the economy: quantitative easing.

rows.title: President Trump's Vision of U.S. Shipbuilding Requires Rebuilding An Industry
rows.standfirst: President Trump wants to bring shipbuilding back to the U.S. to counter China and boost American jobs. The ambitious goal will require rebuilding infrastructure and retraining a workforce. And in Paris, twenty years of discouraging car traffic and planting trees is yielding cleaner air and revitalized river banks and public spaces.

rows.title: Automakers are eating the cost of tariffs — for now
rows.standfirst: Last quarter, tariffs cost the auto industry billions of dollars. So far, that has come out of profits instead of being passed along to buyers. But that could change.

rows.title: The U.S. economy rebounds to 3% growth in second quarter — but tariffs skew picture
rows.standfirst: The U.S. economy grew this spring after a slowdown earlier this year. A report from the Commerce Department shows the nation's GDP grew at an annual rate of 3% in the second quarter of the year.

rows.title: Trump keeps pressuring the Fed to cut rates. Here's why its independence matters
rows.standfirst: Trump has threatened to fire Fed Chair Jerome Powell, challenging the Fed's independence. Experts say he's not the first president to target the central bank, but he's the most public and aggressive.

rows.title: The risk of private equity in your 401(k)
rows.standfirst: Private equity is a risky business. There are high-highs and low-lows. A retirement plan, on the other hand, is meant to be a reliable beast. But President Trump believes your 401(k) can handle it! On today's show, the president's expected executive order could help offer some legal cover for fund managers who include private equity in your retirement portfolio. What are the risks and benefits?

rows.title: The Fed holds interest rates steady despite intense pressure from Trump
rows.standfirst: The Federal Reserve left its benchmark interest rate unchanged Wednesday, but a rate cut is possible in September. President Trump has been urging the central bank to lower borrowing costs.
